From RStudio

If you publish from RStudio today, you can keep doing it. Launchpad answers the same calls Posit Connect does, so the Publish button and rsconnect::deployApp() work unchanged — you add Launchpad as a server once, and from then on you publish to it like any Connect server.

You do not need lp for any of this. RStudio talks to Launchpad through the rsconnect package it already uses.

Before you start

Section titled “Before you start”
  • You need to be a publisher. A viewer can sign in but cannot create content. See Becoming a publisher.
  • Personal API keys must be switched on for your install. Signing RStudio in creates one for you. If adding the account fails before a browser opens, this is the usual reason — ask your administrator.
  • A recent rsconnect. Version 1.0 or later; RStudio updates it with your other packages.

Add Launchpad as a server

Section titled “Add Launchpad as a server”

In RStudio:

  1. Tools → Global Options → Publishing, then Connect…, and choose Posit Connect.
  2. Enter your Launchpad address — the one you sign in to, such as https://launchpad.your-company.com. Leave off any path.
  3. RStudio opens a Launchpad page in your browser titled Sign in RStudio.
  4. Check it, and select Approve.
  5. Back in RStudio, the account finishes adding itself.

What the approval page is asking

Section titled “What the approval page is asking”

Approving creates a personal API key that acts as you — it can deploy, roll back and read anything you can. The page shows the address the request came from and the rsconnect version that asked.

Approve only if you just added the account yourself. Anyone can start a sign-in and send you the link; approving somebody else’s gives them a key that is you. If you did not just do this, select Deny — nothing is created, and the request cannot be reused.

Publish

Section titled “Publish”

Use the Publish button in RStudio, or from the console:

The build log streams into RStudio’s Deploy pane while Launchpad builds the app. When it finishes, RStudio opens the app’s page in Launchpad.

What happens on Launchpad’s side:

  • A new app is created the first time, named after the folder — or after appName if you pass one. That name becomes its address: /apps/<name>/.
  • It starts private. Only you can open it until you share it. See Who can see your app.
  • Your packages come from the bundle. rsconnect records the packages your app uses in a manifest.json, and Launchpad installs exactly those. You do not need an renv.lock for a publish from RStudio. See R.
  • It is an ordinary Launchpad app. Logs, settings, sharing, schedules and rollback all work the way the rest of this guide describes.

Publish again

Section titled “Publish again”

Publish from the same folder and rsconnect updates the same app — it remembers which app it published to. Each publish is a new release, and the previous one keeps serving until the new one is ready. See Releases and rollback.

If the deploy fails, the app keeps serving its last good release, and the build log in the Deploy pane says where it stopped.

Environment variables

Section titled “Environment variables”

Variables you pass to deployApp() are stored on the app:

rsconnect reads each value from your own R session and sends it. Launchpad stores every variable set this way as sensitive: it is never shown back, on the app’s Settings tab or anywhere else. To change one, publish again with a new value, or edit it on the app’s Settings.

What is different from Posit Connect

Section titled “What is different from Posit Connect”

Publishing works the same. Managing the app afterwards happens in Launchpad rather than through rsconnect:

  • Sharing, access and visibility are on the app’s Access tab — not set from RStudio.
  • Custom URLs do not exist. An app’s address is its name.
  • A name already in use is refused, rather than renamed. Pick a different appName.
  • Scheduled re-renders are set up in Launchpad. See Scheduled re-renders.

Signing RStudio out

Section titled “Signing RStudio out”

The key RStudio uses is listed under Me → Credentials as RStudio (rsconnect), with when it was last used. Revoke it there to sign RStudio out; the next publish fails, and RStudio asks you to add the account again.

Like other personal keys it expires after 90 days. When it does, remove the account in RStudio’s Publishing options and add it again.

Posit Workbench

Section titled “Posit Workbench”

Everything above works the same in RStudio on Posit Workbench. The approval page opens in the browser you are using Workbench from.

When it goes wrong

Section titled “When it goes wrong”
What you see What it means
Adding the server fails before a browser opens Personal API keys are switched off for your install. Ask your administrator.
RStudio waits and the approval page never appeared Open the address RStudio prints in its console.
unknown token — add the account again The key behind the account was revoked, expired, or the sign-in was denied. Remove the account and add it again.
the request's Date is … more than five minutes from this server's clock The clock on the machine running RStudio is wrong. Fix it and try again.
the name "…" is already in use Another app has that name. Publish with a different appName.
this key is read-scoped The key you registered with connectApiUser() is read-only. Create a full-scope key, or use the sign-in above instead.
The deploy fails at library() A package your app loads was not recorded in the bundle. Load it at the top of your app and publish again.
